The '''''Star Trek'' Customizable Card Game''' ('''Star Trek CCG''') was [[Decipher]]'s first customizable card game. [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] designed it. Decipher released it in 1994 as ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' Customizable Card Game.<ref name="st-timeline">Kathy McCracken, [http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html The History of Star Trek CCG: The Timeline], Decipher (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080821113824/http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-stccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_Customizable_Card_Game Star Trek Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927114824/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref>

Players scored by completing missions and solving dilemmas along a spaceline of locations.<ref name="duelist3">Deanna Dusbabek, "Star Trek: The Next Generation Customizable Card Game", ''The Duelist'' 3 (Fall 1994), pp. 50–51. [https://archive.org/details/DuelistMagazineIssue3 Internet Archive].</ref> Braunlich and Tesh called location-based play "the central element of all of our CCGs".<ref name="rfd14">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=279s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:39–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Living on Bainbridge Island near Wizards of the Coast, they met ''Magic: The Gathering'' designer [[Richard Garfield]] and told Wizards they would not copy ''Magic''.<ref name="bp27">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref>

== Relation to SWCCG ==

Work on [[Star Wars CCG]] began right after the ''Star Trek'' launch, before the ''Star Wars'' license was signed.<ref name="bp-start">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 3:06–4:40. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Braunlich moved to the ''Star Wars'' game before the ''Star Trek'' game was finished.<ref name="bp27" />

SWCCG kept several ''Star Trek'' ideas: 60-card decks, film stills as card art, a row of locations, a split between "noun" cards (characters and locations) and "verb" cards (interrupts), and a policy of not rotating old cards out.<ref name="bp27" />

[[Bill Martinson]] later led design of the ''Star Trek'' game. He also edited SWCCG card text with [[Warren Holland]].<ref name="darcy-dag">[https://www.kendallcast.ninja/2021/11/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah.html Jerry Darcy on Dagobah], KendallCast (2 November 2021). Audio: [https://archive.org/details/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah Internet Archive]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009004205/https://www.kendallcast.ninja/2021/11/jerry-darcy-on-dagobah.html Internet Archive].</ref>
